title: French: 20 Most Common Verbs
description: Twenty high-frequency French verbs with their English meanings and a short example sentence for each.
subject: languages

cards.definition: To be. Example: Je suis fatigué. (I am tired.)
To have. Example: J'ai un chat. (I have a cat.)
To go. Example: Nous allons au cinéma. (We are going to the movies.)
To do; to make. Example: Il fait ses devoirs. (He is doing his homework.)
To say; to tell. Example: Elle dit bonjour. (She says hello.)
To be able to; can. Example: Je peux venir demain. (I can come tomorrow.)
To want. Example: Je veux du café. (I want some coffee.)
To know (a fact or how to do something). Example: Je sais nager. (I know how to swim.)
To see. Example: Je vois la mer. (I see the sea.)
To come. Example: Elle vient de Paris. (She comes from Paris.)
To have to; must; to owe. Example: Je dois partir. (I have to leave.)
To take. Example: Je prends le bus. (I take the bus.)
To give. Example: Il me donne un livre. (He gives me a book.)
To speak; to talk. Example: Nous parlons français. (We speak French.)
To put; to put on. Example: Mets ton manteau. (Put on your coat.)
To find. Example: Je ne trouve pas mes clés. (I can't find my keys.)
To believe. Example: Je te crois. (I believe you.)
To think. Example: Je pense que oui. (I think so.)
To like; to love. Example: J'aime la musique. (I like music.)
To pass; to spend (time); to stop by. Example: Nous passons l'été ici. (We are spending the summer here.)
